'''Neil J. Calkin''' (born 29 March 1961) is a professor at [[Clemson University]] in the Algebra and Discrete Mathematics group of the School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences.  His interests are in combinatorial and probabilistic methods, mainly as applied to [[number theory]].

Together with [[Herbert Wilf]] he founded [[The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics]] in 1994.<ref>[https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/about About the Journal] The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics</ref> He and Wilf developed the [[Calkin–Wilf tree]] and the associated Calkin–Wilf sequence.<ref>"[http://www.jstor.org/stable/2589182 Recounting the Rationals]", by Neil Calkin and Herbert S. Wilf, [[The American Mathematical Monthly]], Vol. 107, No. 4 (Apr. 2000), pp. 360-363</ref>

==Biography==
Neil Calkin was born 29 March 1961, in [[Hartford, Connecticut]] and moved to the UK around the age of 3.  He grew up there and studied mathematics at [[Trinity College, Cambridge|Trinity College Cambridge]] before moving to Canada in 1984 to study in the Department of Combinatorics and Optimization at the [[University of Waterloo]] where he was awarded a PhD (1988) for his thesis "Sum-Free Sets and Measure Spaces" written under the supervision of [[Ian Peter Goulden]].<ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=43628 Neil Calkin] at the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]</ref>

He was the [[Zeev Nehari]] Visiting Assistant Professor of Mathematics at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] (1988—1991), an assistant professor at [[Georgia Tech]] (1991—1997),<ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Neil-Calkin|Neil Calkin] ResearchGate</ref> and joined the Algebra and Discrete Mathematics group of the School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences at Clemson University in 1997.<ref>[https://www.clemson.edu/science/departments/math-stat/directory/profiles/calkin Mathematical and Statistical Sciences: Neil Calkin] Clemson University</ref>

Calkin has an [[Erdős number]] of 1.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Calkin | first1=Neil J.
| last2=Erdős | first2=Paul | authorlink2=Paul Erdős
| title=On a class of aperiodic sum-free sets
| journal=[[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]]
| volume=120
| issue=1
| date=1996
| pages=1-5
| doi=10.1017/S0305004100074600| hdl=1853/31264
| hdl-access=free
}}</ref> He was one of the last people to collaborate with [[Paul Erdős|Erdős]] and once said of him, "One of my greatest regrets is that I didn't know him when he was a million times faster than most people. When I knew him he was only hundreds of times faster."<ref>''My Brain Is Open : The Mathematical Journeys of Paul Erdos'' (1998) by Bruce Schechter, p. 119</ref>
